message:
Manager, Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer and Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, my single chain still decides holding and I confirm it for version three.

In plain words cold heat is not wire power until divided by hot efficiency, with one door leak counted once. Reusing interior 8.64 cubic metres from the interior volume estimate (E39) with envelope 25.4 square metres from the envelope area square metres (E40) giving conduction 203 Watt from the conduction watts at 43C ambient 5C room (E41), my single thermal total conduction respiration door pulldown fans (E109) at 13.5 kilowatt-hour thermal per day names conduction 4.87 plus respiration 1.20 plus door 0.169 plus staged pull-down 6.25 for 250 kilogram per day plus fans 0.96, which supersedes 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day from the steady plus staged pull-down daily kWh (E58) and 12.8 kilowatt-hour thermal per day from the thermal cooling total kWh_th per day conduction plus respiration plus door plus staged pull-down (E92). My single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) at 0.169 kilowatt-hour per day for 8 openings with curtain plus latent supersedes 0.440 kilowatt-hour per day from the door infiltration kWh per day for 4 air changes (E57). Divided by Coefficient of Performance (COP, cooling per electric power) 1.40 hot plus controls 0.48 equals 10.4 kilowatt-hour electrical per day from the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111), about one household day so everyday scale holds, leaving about 3.10 kilowatt-hour margin to 13.5 kilowatt-hour per day yield.

In plain words thick light foam buys small leak, a one-crate door keeps the hole small, and village service beats a small efficiency gain. From my discipline the Insulated PUR PIR Sandwich Panel 100mm Cold Room Panels Roof Cladding (E116) that Enclosure and Structural Designer put on the board confirms buildability, because 12.1 kilogram per square metre at 100 millimetre giving about 306 kilogram on that envelope buys U about 0.21 Watt per square metre Kelvin and that 203 Watt leak, about two old light bulbs so everyday scale holds. The Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) that Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist put on the board states 900 millimetre standard doors, which I confirm keeps the single door model true because it passes one 600 millimetre by 400 millimetre crate at a time with Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC, flexible plastic) curtain clamped to rigid Polyisocyanurate (PIR, rigid foam insulation). R134a (tetrafluoroethane, A1 non-flammable refrigerant) over R290 (propane, A3 flammable refrigerant) from R134a vs. R290 Refrigerant: Key Differences and Replacements (E17) with hot rating from BD50F Direct Current Compressor R134a, 12-24V DC and 100-240V AC 50/60Hz (E102) justifies derated COP 1.40 at 43 degrees Celsius ambient.

Manager, high rear to low return uniformity and 43 degree pull-down timing still need built hardware and I name them as bench test, not proven here, with full 1000 kilogram warm at once needing 25.0 kilowatt-hour from the recompute sensible pull-down because E12 looks off by units (E26) refused by your staged 12.5 crates per day rule.

My position is ready on version three, because thermal to electrical conversion, single curtain door model and serviceable hot refrigerant now close with joint numbers.
